title: Any employee can approve leave requests, including their own
summary: The approve action checks nothing about who is calling it. Any logged-in employee can approve their own leave request or a colleague's, so the manager's approval step can be skipped completely.
steps: POST /api/requests {start:'2031-05-06', end:'2031-05-06'} → pending request id N
Also: log in as cleo@acme.example (employee) and POST /api/requests/M/approve on Ben's request M

expected.text: HTTP 403 for anyone who is not a manager or who owns the request; request stays pending.

actual: HTTP 200, status becomes 'approved' with decided_by = the employee (Ben himself, or Cleo).

how.response: POST /api/requests/1/approve as Ben → 200 {status:'approved', decided_by:2}; POST /api/requests/2/approve as Cleo → 200 {status:'approved', decided_by:3}
how.state: SELECT status, decided_by FROM requests WHERE id IN (1,2) → approved/2 (Ben himself), approved/3 (Cleo, an employee)
how.byDesignCheck: R4 says only a manager can approve and nobody can decide their own request; rejectRequest right below has exactly these checks, approveRequest lacks them.

hint: In approveRequest add the same two checks as rejectRequest: role must be 'manager' (403) and req.user_id !== user.id (403).
